research_rationale:
basis_pattern: original_plus_bounded_search. EO 14085 (signed 2022-10-03; 87 FR 60541; official Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_14085.txt, read in full) amends six earlier orders on military decorations and awards (EO 9158 Air Medal, EO 8809 Good Conduct Medal, EO 10694 unit citations, EO 11046 Bronze Star Medal, EO 13830 delegation of authority to approve decorations, EO 11545 Defense Distinguished Service Medal) to cover the Space Force and to use gender-neutral and updated wording, and adds general provisions. Identity: heading, title and date agree with the register row. The dossier inventory fragmented the sections, so I replaced it with eight clauses (inventory override). Own terms: no section has an end date or ending condition. Later instruments: a search of held order texts for the number 14085 finds only the order's own Federal Register copy; the dossier chain lists no event, and the ofr_catalog search records no disposition note naming it. Current law: the U.S. Code (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; laws of 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14 not reflected) prints each amended order with a status line naming EO 14085: EO 9158 as amended by section 1, EO 8809 by section 2, EO 10694 by section 3, EO 11046 by section 4, EO 13830 by section 5 (notes under 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, pt. II, ch. 57) and EO 11545 by section 6 (note under 10 U.S.C. 1125) (jobs/current-law/output/MENTIONS.csv, USC_EO_NOTES.jsonl); the amended orders are therefore printed as current text with the amendments embodied. One caution is stated plainly: the Code's editorial note under 10 U.S.C. 7276 records that section 4(a) of EO 14085 (substituting Homeland Security for Transportation in paragraph 1 of EO 11046) could not be executed because EO 13286 had already made the identical amendment; section 4(b) to (d) are not affected by that note, and the clause for section 4 is claimed operative on the strength of those paragraphs and the printed amended text, not on 4(a). The order cites no statute as its authority (the Constitution and the laws generally, and the President's office as Commander in Chief); the Code sections the amended orders refer to are not held and I assert nothing about them. The three selected machine searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) were read with their coverage notes; none carries a coverage warning and none records a revocation or supersession of EO 14085.
